heading: Cheap Eats in Kelowna
title: Cheap Eats in Kelowna | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to eat well for less in Kelowna: diner breakfasts, banh mi and subs, pho and curry, food-truck tacos, bakeries, late-night slices and vegan picks.
intro: You don't need a big budget to eat well in Kelowna. This guide sticks to independent, mostly family-run and owner-run places: diners, sandwich counters, pho shops, food trucks, bakeries and late-night slice shops. Most are the cheapest price level on our site, and the few that aren't are here because their listings single out the value.

The picks spread across downtown, Pandosy, Rutland, Glenmore and the Lower Mission. Food trucks and patio spots often cut back their hours from November to April, so check each listing's hours before you head out.

sections.heading: Breakfast for less
sections.lead: For a sit-down brunch with all the trimmings, see our {page:/guides/best-brunch-kelowna|best brunch in Kelowna guide}. These are the easier-on-the-wallet mornings.

items.name: Norman's Diner
items.text: an old-fashioned diner that regulars call one of the most welcoming, affordable family breakfast spots in town. Prices haven't crept up the way they have elsewhere.

items.name: Pulp Fiction
items.text: a coffee house that doubles as a rare and used bookstore, with a strong breakfast menu. Order the coffee milkshake regulars rave about and browse while you eat.

items.name: The Sandwich Company
items.text: a breakfast-and-lunch sandwich shop with a loyal following, anchored by a well-loved breakfast burrito. There are proper vegan options too.

items.name: Specialty Bakery & Bistro
items.text: a scratch bakery with a bistro serving all-day breakfast and daily lunch specials on weekdays. Grab a cream-filled Kelonut on the way out.

items.name: Little Hobo Soup & Sandwich Shop
items.text: a hole-in-the-wall that's been a local staple since the 1970s. Order the grilled cheese or the three-soup flight. More bowls like this are in our {page:/guides/soup-ramen-pho-okanagan|soup, ramen and pho guide}.

items.name: Banh Mi Bo Bakery
items.text: a dedicated banh mi bakery with baguettes baked fresh daily and a focused menu. Start with the classic.

items.name: Italian Sandwich Co.
items.text: easy to walk past in a food court near the office district, but the sandwiches are built with imported meats and cheeses.

items.name: Rocket Subs
items.text: a small sub shop with a cult following for fresh ingredients and generous portions. It can sell out on weekends, so arrive early.

items.name: Press'd Sandwich Shop
items.text: an owner-run shop near Landmark. Order one of the creatively named signature sandwiches.

items.name: Wood Fire Bakery
items.text: a German bakery-cafe with generous portions and fair prices. It's open weekdays only for a short midday window, so plan ahead and order the borscht and ham hock.

sections.heading: Noodles, pho and curry
sections.lead: Big bowls that go a long way. Our {page:/guides/soup-ramen-pho-okanagan|soup, ramen and pho guide} covers the whole valley.

items.name: Bamboo Chopsticks Downtown
items.text: a vegan-friendly Vietnamese spot with big portions for the price. The customizable pho is what regulars swear by.

items.name: Basil Leaf Asian Fusion
items.text: quick, affordable Vietnamese-Thai food. Order the pho, whose broth tastes like it took hours.

items.name: Natsukashi Neighbourhood Store & Eatery
items.text: a nostalgic Japanese corner store stocked with snacks, where you can sit down for bowls of udon and fresh onigiri.

items.name: Yellow Star Snack House
items.text: a casual Vietnamese spot for banh mi, vermicelli bowls, spring rolls and bao buns, with kind staff and vegetarian options.

items.name: Made in India
items.text: a budget-friendly Indian restaurant that suits families and groups. Reviewers mention butter chicken, rogan josh, korma and garlic naan.

items.name: Pick Thai Restaurant
items.text: a small, family-run spot on Bernard Ave where mom does the cooking, so every dish tastes homemade.

items.name: Charros Takos
items.text: street tacos from a food truck, on fresh handmade corn tortillas. Try the tofu pastor and the bean soup on the side.

items.name: Streats Harvey Kitchen
items.text: a smash burger and taco counter. The cauliflower tacos and crispy halloumi make it good for vegetarians too.

items.name: The Hot Box
items.text: a smash burger and smoked BBQ food truck by the bike path, a favourite pit stop for cyclists and walkers.

items.name: Latin Fiesta
items.text: affordable, authentic Latin American food. Order the chilaquiles or the pozole, and there's a proper kids' menu.

items.name: Pandosy Pizza
items.text: known for a homemade-tasting tomato sauce on a generous, non-greasy pie.

items.name: Panjabi Pizzeria
items.text: halal Indian-fusion pizza with dine-in tables. Reviewers say the Achari Chicken pizza is worth the wait.

items.name: 350° Bakehouse and Cafe
items.text: a from-scratch bakery for donuts, cronuts, lemon tarts, scones and sausage rolls, plus deli sandwiches and a daily soup.

items.name: Jaide & Joel's Baking Co.
items.text: fresh baking, lunch options and coffee, with free parking behind the building.

items.name: Tripke Bakery Too
items.text: big muffins, flaky pastries, sausage rolls and a good selection of gluten-free treats, close to a walking trail.

items.name: Milk Shed Coffeehouse
items.text: a heritage barn attached to a brewery, with cinnamon buns famous enough to justify the trip.

items.name: Empire Crepe
items.text: a family-run counter that makes everything hot to order. Start savory, then finish with the salted caramel crepe.

items.name: City Pizza
items.text: open past midnight, with slices on a light sauce and a fluffy crust. It's well loved for supporting the local homeless community with warm meals.

items.name: Halfmoon Pizzeria + Donair
items.text: pizza and donair under one roof, and neither feels like an afterthought. Order one of each.

items.name: MASHAWI - Shawarma & Grill
items.text: authentic Turkish food from a hardworking young couple, open well past typical dinner hours, with generous portions.

items.name: King's Vegetarian Food
items.text: a beloved, family-run market stall. Order the sweet and sour veggie and add a few steamed buns.

items.name: Eye Tasty Food
items.text: an Ethiopian food truck run by a husband-and-wife team, with fresh, healthy home cooking worth seeking out.

items.name: reggaefusionfood
items.text: a food truck with live music playing. The chickpea curry is well loved.

items.name: Goods Health and Wellness
items.text: a wellness store and smoothie bar run by people who know the vegan landscape well, with a bring-your-own-cup option.

items.tip: trucks move and markets change their schedules with the season, so check each listing before you go.
